text:
Jordan: quick q — ACME just requested a full account erase (GDPR). Do we need to scrub request logs, traces, and edge caches, or do we only block-profile data?
Maria: short answer: depends on what's in each store. We need the customer ticket + legal signoff before any destructive ops. but yes, traces/logs/edge caches can contain identifiers and typically need action.
Jordan: understood. What are the concrete steps? I'm not sure which teams to pull in.
ops-bot: FYI there is an automated gdpr-erase job but it only covers S3 buckets + Cloud Storage for the last 90 days and only objects tagged with `gdpr_deletable:true`. Older/backfilled logs are manual.
Maria: concrete breakdown: 1) Logs (Cloud Logging): filter by customer_id or requestor_id, export keys, then call the delete API or run scrub job. 2) Traces (Tempo): if you can provide trace_ids/time range we can delete spans; otherwise retention TTL applies. 3) Edge caches/CDN: invalidate paths tied to the customer (fast). 4) Analytics/warehouse: must anonymize or drop rows — coordinate with analytics. 5) Backups: log DB backups need legal approval before touching.
Jordan: any quick commands or runbooks to point to?
Maria: runbook gist (high-level) — use internal script to gather candidates, then ops runs deletion:```bash
# collect keys
python infra/scripts/gdpr_collect.py --customer ACME-123 --from 2022-01-01 --to 2024-12-31 --out /tmp/acme-erase.json
# run scrub (requires infra approval)
python infra/scripts/gdpr_scrub.py --input /tmp/acme-erase.json --confirm
```
Lee: note on CDN: you can invalidate using CloudFront/Cloudflare API. e.g. CloudFront:
```
aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id E2XXX --paths "/accounts/ACME-123/*"
```
Anika: analytics note — we can't just delete rows if they're used in aggregate tables without recompute. plan: anonymize PII fields and mark the user as erased, then run a downstream job to recompute aggregates if necessary. I'll ping analytics.
Jordan: I'll open a ticket with the customer_id, time range, and any trace_ids we can pull. tagging infra + legal. ticket: ENG-4821 (wip)
Maria: perfect. Add "legal:gdpr-erase" label and include this checklist in the ticket body. also include whether backups need exemption.
ops-bot: infra note — manual backfill deletions require a runbook sign-off and will be scheduled in the maintenance window. Expect ~2-3 hours for a full backfill depending on range.
Lee: security approval: once legal signs off I can approve the scrub for Tempo and logging. please include me on the ticket.
Jordan: done — ENG-4821 updated with time range and some sample trace_ids. tagging @Maria @Lee @Anika.
Maria: I'll review and then we can schedule the scrub. keep snapshots of the collected keys in a secure folder and don't post them in public channels. :white_check_mark:
Anika: pinged analytics and will follow up in the ticket with recommended anonymization steps.
Maria: summary for the ticket body (you can copy):
- customer_id: ACME-123
- time_range: 2022-01-01 -> 2024-12-31
- data_sources: request-logs (Cloud Logging), traces (Tempo), CDN caches (CloudFront), analytics warehouse, backups
- immediate actions: freeze exports, collect candidate keys (gdpr_collect.py), request legal approval
- post-approval actions: run gdpr_scrub.py (infra), invalidate CDN paths, anonymize analytics, record audit entry
Jordan: thanks all — will wait for legal then move forward.
Maria: thanks — keep all discussion in ENG-4821 from now on.
